title: Quasi-compactness and the absolute structure morphism of a stack
statement: Work with schemes [def-pc-scheme], universes [def-weil-size-convention], algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and the morphisms and $2$-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of stack morphisms use [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Let $\mathcal A$ be an algebraic stack over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $p:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ be its structure morphism. Then $\mathcal A$ admits a smooth surjective atlas from a quasi-compact scheme if and only if $p$ is quasi-compact: for every quasi-compact algebraic stack $\mathcal V$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, the stack $\mathcal A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathcal V$ is quasi-compact. No quasi-separatedness hypothesis on $\mathcal A$ or on $\mathcal V$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), affine smooth atlases and surjective images; Tag 050U (definition-quasi-compact), applied to the absolute structure morphism. The product of affine atlases over Spec Z is affine (schemes.tex Tag 01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affines).

proof.text: Write $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. A scheme $T$ gives the discrete stack $h_T$: its diagonal is represented by scheme fibre products, and its identity is an etale surjective scheme atlas by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], hence a smooth one by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. If $T$ is quasi-compact, that identity atlas makes $h_T$ quasi-compact by [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. In particular $Z$ is a quasi-compact algebraic stack, since it is affine and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] gives quasi-compactness. Suppose $p$ is quasi-compact. Its defining test with $Z\xrightarrow{1}Z$ gives that $\mathcal A\times_Z Z$ is quasi-compact. In the triple description of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], projection onto $\mathcal A$ is an equivalence: the inverse sends $x$ to $(x,p(x),1)$, and the isomorphism in a triple identifies its other component with $p(x)$. Thus $\mathcal A$ has the required quasi-compact scheme atlas.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $\mathcal A$ has a quasi-compact smooth surjective scheme atlas, and fix an arbitrary quasi-compact algebraic stack $\mathcal V$ over $Z$. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-quasicompact-surjection], applied separately to $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal V$, choose smooth surjective atlases $a:U\to\mathcal A$ and $b:W\to\mathcal V$ with $U,W$ affine. Both maps are representable by algebraic spaces by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products], $\mathcal P=\mathcal A\times_Z\mathcal V$ and $U\times_Z\mathcal V$ are algebraic stacks.

source.place: Tags 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), 050U (definition-quasi-compact), 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines), 0302/0301 (base change/composition of representable maps), 045C/045B (base change/composition of their properties)

proof.text: The map $q:U\times_ZW\to\mathcal P$ factors as $U\times_ZW\to U\times_Z\mathcal V\to\mathcal A\times_Z\mathcal V$. The first arrow is the base change of $b$ along $U\times_Z\mathcal V\to\mathcal V$; the second is the base change of $a$ along $\mathcal P\to\mathcal A$. The identifications follow directly from the triple description of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: the extra component and its specified isomorphism are forgotten, and the inverse inserts the forced component with identity isomorphism. By the base-change and composition clauses of [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus], $q$ is representable, smooth and surjective.

source.place: Tags 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), 050U (definition-quasi-compact), 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines), 0302/0301 (base change/composition of representable maps), 045C/045B (base change/composition of their properties)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], writing $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$, the source of $q$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B)$. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus $q$ is a smooth surjective atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, so $\mathcal P$ is quasi-compact by [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Since $\mathcal V$ was arbitrary, the same definition says $p$ is quasi-compact. Only the base $Z$ and the two chosen atlas schemes were required to be affine; no diagonal of $\mathcal A$ or $\mathcal V$ was assumed quasi-compact or quasi-separated.
